title: Editor result
description: v0.1. What `python -m diocle_converter editor check|convert` prints on stdout for the VS Code extension (editors/vscode). LOCAL use only: the developer runs it on their own machine with their own Meta key, so diagnostics carry the compiler's full message and real line numbers (unlike compile-check.schema.json, which is the sanitized form for visitor imports and never echoes source). Progress goes to stderr as `PROGRESS <text>` lines; stdout holds exactly one JSON document of this shape. For `convert` this record only POINTS at the run: the run record (run.schema.json, v0.14) stays the source of truth for the assurance, reason, cost and model, and is copied, not re-derived. `assurance` is `certified` only when the Java matched the original COBOL byte for byte on the inputs tried (not a proof); the other labels are never to be shown as certified. `skipped` means no conversion was attempted (not convertible without convert-anyway, or an unreadable input).

ok.description: check: the file compiles under cobc -std=ibm. convert: the command ran to a record (false only when it could not start, e.g. no cobc or no key); the outcome is `assurance`.

file.description: The file as given on the command line.

error.description: Why the command could not produce its normal result (cobc missing, no model key, bad input). Never contains a key.

file.description: Path as cobc printed it (may be a copybook).

assuranceReason.description: Copied from run.json assuranceReason, or the reason for `skipped`.

runDir.description: Absolute path of the folder holding the copied run (run.json, java/, ...).

files.description: Absolute paths of what exists; a key is absent when that artefact was not produced.

diff.description: Unified diff, original COBOL to patched COBOL, as written by the repair step.

maxUsd.description: The hard dollar cap this run was given.
